findings.title: Timestamp insertion path violates the stated canonicalization rule
findings.evidence: Section 4.1: "The same normalized string MUST be used for both the INSERT parameter and the hash input." Section 7: `Timestamp = turn.Timestamp, CanonicalTimestamp = canonicalTimestamp, // Used for hash input`
findings.problem: The code path still stores the raw `turn.Timestamp` while hashing `canonicalTimestamp`. That contradicts the spec's own requirement and leaves DB persistence dependent on Npgsql/Postgres timestamp normalization behavior rather than the canonical value used for hashing.
findings.why_it_matters: A non-UTC or sub-microsecond input can round/truncate differently on insert than in the hash input, causing recomputed hashes to diverge after round-trip and making validation nondeterministic across environments.
findings.proposed_fix: Normalize `turn.Timestamp` to a concrete UTC microsecond-precision value before constructing `DhfEntryRecord`, use that exact normalized value for the DB parameter and for hash computation, and add an integration test covering non-UTC offsets and 7-digit fractional ticks.

findings.title: Session close/split operations are not coordinated with append operations
findings.evidence: Section 6.1: `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(@k))` with `lockKey = $"dhf_session_open:{metadata.WorkstationId}"`; Section 7: `lockKey = $"dhf_append:{turn.SessionId}"`; Section 6.2 only says `CloseSessionAsync(sessionId)` sets `ended_at = NOW()`.
findings.problem: Open/resume/close uses a workstation-scoped lock, while append uses a session-scoped lock. These lock domains do not coordinate, so a session can be closed or split while an append is in flight. `AppendTurnAsync` also has no retry path for serialization failures.
findings.why_it_matters: This can drop turns on transient `40001` errors or allow commits that the application semantically considers post-close, depending on transaction interleaving.
findings.proposed_fix: Make close/split acquire the same per-session lock(s) used by append, or lock the target session rows consistently (`FOR UPDATE`) before both close and append decisions; add bounded retry handling for serialization failures in `AppendTurnAsync`.

findings.title: The supersede decoration model has no write interface
findings.evidence: SDR-04-002: "new decoration rows may reference `supersedes_decoration_id` to logically replace a prior decoration". Section 8 writer signature: `WriteDecorationAsync(Guid entryId, DecorationType type, JsonElement payload, string createdBy, CancellationToken ct)` and INSERT omits `supersedes_decoration_id`.
findings.problem: The spec requires insert-with-supersede behavior, but the only defined writer API cannot supply the prior decoration ID or express replacement semantics.
findings.why_it_matters: The declared data model cannot be implemented or tested as written, and readers have no contract for resolving which decoration is current after replacement.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit supersede-capable API/parameter, define validation rules for replacement, and define the read contract for active-vs-superseded decorations.

findings.title: Integrity-event deduplication is contradictory and not enforceable under concurrency
findings.evidence: Section 8.2: "it checks for an existing `integrity_event` decoration of the same `eventType` on the same entry before inserting a new one. If an identical event already exists, no new row is written." The table/index definition has no unique constraint supporting that rule.
findings.problem: The dedup rule alternates between `same eventType` and `identical event`, which are not the same key. There is also no unique index or upsert strategy, so concurrent deep validations can still insert duplicates.
findings.why_it_matters: Dedup behavior becomes nondeterministic: distinct failures can be collapsed if they share an `eventType`, or duplicate rows can appear under concurrent validation runs.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a single dedup key explicitly (for example `entry_id + eventType + decoration_hash`) and enforce it with a unique index plus `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.

findings.title: Cross-workstation collision handling can terminate another active session based on an untrusted identifier
findings.evidence: SDR-04-008: "This assumes `workstation_id` is a stable, non-spoofed machine identifier" and "A spoofed or colliding `workstation_id` can cause one orchestrator to prematurely close another's sessions." Section 6.1: "Same AddinSessionId on a DIFFERENT workstation... Close the stale session before opening a new one."
findings.problem: The implementation automatically closes an existing open session on another workstation when `addin_session_id` matches, even though the trust boundary is explicitly acknowledged as spoofable/collidable.
findings.why_it_matters: A collision or spoof can silently split another workstation's ledger session and misattribute or interrupt writes, which is hard to detect after the fact.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not auto-close cross-workstation conflicts. Reject them as a recoverable error or require a stronger authenticated machine/instance identity before allowing one workstation to close another's session.

top_3_must_fix: Use the exact same normalized UTC microsecond timestamp value for both hash input and DB insertion.
Coordinate session close/split with append using the same locking/retry model.
Define and enforce a real integrity-event dedup key with a DB constraint/upsert path.
